title: db.pitr.base — a physical base backup for point-in-time recovery (`falak-db backup physical`: pg_basebackup -Ft -X none, xtrabackup / mariadb-backup xbstream) through zstd and AES-256-GCM (FKB1) to a presigned URL; mysql/mariadb close the binlog being written first, and after a binlog reset spooling restarts (`binlog-rotate --restart`)

volume_id.description: the instance's volume: the base turns shipping on itself (pitr.json) under the instance's lock, so the WAL it needs is never emptied from the spool

uncompressed_bytes.description: the dump's size (a Redis / Valkey restore gets it back as uncompressed_bytes)

plaintext_sha256.description: the plaintext's SHA-256 (authenticated in the file's trailer)

started_at.description: falak-db's start (the server's clock, like the segments' end times)

start_wal.description: postgres: the first WAL segment the base needs

stop_wal.description: postgres: the last WAL segment the base needs (in the spool when the backup returned)

start_binlog.description: mysql/mariadb: the binlog being written when the base started (closed just before it)

encryption.description: FKB1 (docs/BACKUPS.md): zstd, then AES-256-GCM in 64 KiB segments with a random 32-byte data key per backup. cp: the control plane generated the key (wrapped under the organization's key on its side) and sends it here; age: the agent generates it and stores it in the file's header, encrypted to the customer's X25519 recipient (the control plane never sees it)

key_id.description: the backup's key id (its id): written in the file's header and checked when it is opened

key.description: secret: the 32-byte data key, base64 (or hex). The agent keeps it in memory only

key_id.description: the backup's key id (its id): written in the file's header and checked when it is opened

recipient.description: the customer's age X25519 recipient (public key)
